guideTitle: The Best Chair Mats for High-Pile and Extra-Thick Carpet
breadcrumbLabel: Best Chair Mats for High Pile Carpet
metaTitle: Best Chair Mats for High Pile Carpet: Pile Ratings Compared (2026)
metaDescription: We compared chair mats for thick carpet by pile rating, cleat design, rigidity, size and warranty, and explain which mats are rated for extra-high pile and which only reach 3/4 inch.
introParagraphs: On thick carpet, a standard chair mat sinks almost as soon as you sit down, and the casters end up pressing into the fibers rather than rolling. A mat for deep carpet needs either long cleats that reach through the pile to grip the backing, or enough rigidity to bridge the pile without flexing, and ideally a pile rating that matches your carpet.

Pile ratings are the key number, and they vary more than product names suggest. Only two mats here, both from ES Robbins, are rated for extra-high pile over 1 inch including padding. Several others are rated up to 3/4 inch, and the glass and 5mm rigid mats rely on stiffness rather than a specific pile rating.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, including pile rating, size, thickness, capacity and warranty, plus price position, not hands-on testing. Measure your carpet before choosing.

es-robbins-extra-high-pile-lip.summary: A 36 x 48-inch vinyl mat with a lip, rated for pile over 1 inch including padding, with a lifetime warranty.
es-robbins-extra-high-pile-lip.description:
The ES Robbins Extra High Pile mat is the one to start with if your carpet is genuinely deep: it is rated for extra-high pile over 1 inch including padding, and its AnchorBar cleats are designed to reach through to the backing.

It is 0.2-inch vinyl in a standard 36 x 48-inch size with a lip, and adds a beveled edge. ES Robbins lists GREENGUARD Gold certification, US manufacturing and a lifetime warranty.

The standard size may feel tight at a large desk; the Everlife version is larger at a higher price.
specs: Rated for: extra-high pile over 1" including padding
es-robbins-extra-high-pile-lip.bestFor: Standard desks on extra-high pile or padded carpet.
es-robbins-extra-high-pile-lip.skipIf: Your chair covers a wider area; the Everlife extra-high pile mat is 45 x 53 inches.

es-robbins-everlife-extra-high-pile-larg.summary: The same extra-high pile rating in a 45 x 53-inch size with a large lip.
es-robbins-everlife-extra-high-pile-larg.description:
The ES Robbins Everlife extra-high pile mat carries the same over-1-inch rating as the standard version in a larger 45 x 53-inch size with a 25 x 12-inch lip.

On deep pile, a larger mat gives the chair more room before a caster drops off the edge. ES Robbins describes it as built for multi-shift use and backs it with a lifetime "No Crack" warranty. It uses the same AnchorBar cleats and beveled edge.

It costs about $25 more than the standard size at the time of writing and has fewer buyer reviews.
cons: Costs more than the standard size
es-robbins-everlife-extra-high-pile-larg.bestFor: Larger desks on extra-high pile carpet.
es-robbins-everlife-extra-high-pile-larg.skipIf: A 36 x 48-inch mat covers your chair's range; the standard ES Robbins costs less.

es-robbins-everlife-medium-pile-large.summary: A 60 x 72-inch vinyl mat for carpet up to 3/4 inch, for shared or large work areas.
es-robbins-everlife-medium-pile-large.description:
The ES Robbins EverLife medium-pile mat is for large work areas rather than deep carpet: at 60 x 72 inches it is the biggest mat here, but it is rated for carpet only up to 3/4 inch.

That suits a shared desk, an L-shaped desk or a chair that moves between two work surfaces. It has AnchorBar cleats, GREENGUARD certification, US manufacturing and a lifetime "No Crack" warranty.

It is the most expensive mat here at the time of writing and needs a lot of floor. Measure your carpet: if it is deeper than 3/4 inch, choose one of the extra-high-pile mats.
es-robbins-everlife-medium-pile-large.bestFor: Large or shared work areas on carpet up to 3/4 inch.
es-robbins-everlife-medium-pile-large.skipIf: Your carpet is deeper than 3/4 inch; the ES Robbins extra-high-pile mats are rated for it.

muarts-crystal-clear-high-pile.summary: A 5mm rigid clear mat rated for 1,400 lb that relies on stiffness rather than cleats.
muarts-crystal-clear-high-pile.description:
The MuArts is the lowest-cost option here: a 5mm rigid panel that relies on stiffness rather than cleats to avoid sinking, with a listed 1,400 lb capacity.

It works on carpet or hard floors, which helps if you move rooms. The listing does not give a pile rating, and without cleats it is better suited to medium or moderately thick carpet than to very deep pile.

Its 54 x 32-inch shape is wide but shallow, so check how far your chair rolls back from the desk.
muarts-crystal-clear-high-pile.bestFor: Medium or moderately thick carpet on a budget.
muarts-crystal-clear-high-pile.skipIf: Your carpet is over 1 inch deep; the ES Robbins extra-high-pile mats are designed for it.

gorilla-grip-polycarbonate-high-pile.badge: Best Ships-Flat Mat for Carpet up to 3/4 Inch
gorilla-grip-polycarbonate-high-pile.summary: A 36 x 48-inch spiked polycarbonate mat that ships flat, for carpet up to 3/4 inch.
gorilla-grip-polycarbonate-high-pile.description:
The Gorilla Grip polycarbonate mat suits carpet at the top of the medium range: a 36 x 48-inch mat with hundreds of underside spikes, rated for low and medium pile up to 3/4 inch.

It ships flat rather than rolled, so there is no waiting for it to settle, and the semi-transparent finish shows the carpet through.

It is not rated for pile deeper than 3/4 inch, and at 0.087 inches it is thinner than the Marvelux.
gorilla-grip-polycarbonate-high-pile.bestFor: Carpet up to 3/4 inch at a standard desk.
gorilla-grip-polycarbonate-high-pile.skipIf: Your carpet is deeper than 3/4 inch; choose an extra-high-pile ES Robbins mat.

marvelux-polycarbonate-heavy-duty-high-p.summary: A 48 x 60-inch, 0.11-inch polycarbonate mat with studs, rated for carpet up to 3/4 inch.
marvelux-polycarbonate-heavy-duty-high-p.description:
The Marvelux is the larger, thicker polycarbonate option: 48 x 60 inches at 0.11 inches, with a studded underside and a lightly textured top, rated for carpet up to 3/4 inch.

Polycarbonate's stiffness helps on thick carpet, and the larger size gives more room to roll. Marvelux states it is made using 50 percent renewable energy and is recyclable.

Like the Gorilla Grip, it is not rated beyond 3/4 inch, and it has fewer buyer reviews than the vinyl mats.
marvelux-polycarbonate-heavy-duty-high-p.bestFor: Larger desk areas on carpet up to 3/4 inch.
marvelux-polycarbonate-heavy-duty-high-p.skipIf: Your carpet is deeper than 3/4 inch; the ES Robbins extra-high-pile mats are rated for it.

koonmi-tempered-glass-high-pile.summary: A 46 x 55-inch tempered glass mat with a repositionable anti-slip pad.
koonmi-tempered-glass-high-pile.description:
The Koonmi is the glass option for a large area: 46 x 55 inches of 5mm tempered glass, rated for over 1,000 lb, with a detachable anti-slip pad and rounded corners.

Glass is stiff enough to bridge carpet without flexing and works on hard floors too. On very deep or uneven pile, though, a heavy rigid panel may be harder to keep level than a cleated mat, and the listing gives no pile rating.

It is one of the more expensive mats here at the time of writing.
koonmi-tempered-glass-high-pile.bestFor: Large desk areas on medium carpet where a glass surface is preferred.
koonmi-tempered-glass-high-pile.skipIf: Your carpet is extra-high pile; a cleated ES Robbins mat is designed for it.

glsland-tempered-glass-high-pile.summary: A 36 x 46-inch tempered glass mat rated for 1,200 lb.
glsland-tempered-glass-high-pile.description:
The GLSLAND is the lower-cost glass mat: 36 x 46 inches of 5mm tempered glass rated for 1,200 lb, with four anti-slip pads.

It works on carpet or hard floors and is listed as BPA- and phthalate-free. It costs about the same as the MuArts at the time of writing.

Like the Koonmi, it gives no pile rating and relies on stiffness, so it is better suited to medium carpet than to the deepest pile.
glsland-tempered-glass-high-pile.bestFor: Budget buyers on medium carpet who want a glass surface.
glsland-tempered-glass-high-pile.skipIf: Your carpet is over 1 inch deep; choose an extra-high-pile ES Robbins mat.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Measure the carpet to the backing, including any padding. Here, only the two ES Robbins extra-high-pile mats are rated beyond 1 inch; the Gorilla Grip, Marvelux and ES Robbins medium-pile mats top out at 3/4 inch; the glass and MuArts mats give no rating.
Cleated vinyl grips through the pile; rigid polycarbonate, glass and 5mm panels resist flexing. On very deep carpet, a mat rated for that depth is the safer choice.
On thick carpet, rolling off the edge is harder to recover from, so a larger mat helps. Sizes here run from 36 x 46 inches to 60 x 72 inches.
The ES Robbins mats list lifetime warranties and GREENGUARD certification; check other listings for warranty terms.

faq.q: How do I know if my carpet counts as high pile?
faq.a: Push a ruler into the carpet until it meets the backing and measure. Include any padding if the mat's rating does. Compare that figure directly with each mat's pile rating rather than relying on labels like "thick" or "plush".

faq.q: Why did my regular mat stop working on thicker carpet?
faq.a: A mat designed for low pile is thin, with short cleats. On deeper carpet it flexes and sinks, so the chair has nothing firm to roll on.

faq.q: Do I need a special mat for shag carpet?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a mat explicitly rated for extra-high pile, such as the ES Robbins Extra High Pile mats here. Thickness alone does not guarantee a mat will work on very deep carpet.

faq.q: Is glass or polycarbonate better for thick carpet?
faq.a: Both are rigid. The polycarbonate mats here state pile ratings up to 3/4 inch; the glass mats do not state a rating and are heavy, so they are better suited to medium carpet. For the deepest carpet, a mat rated for extra-high pile is the more predictable choice.

faq.q: Is office carpet different from home carpet?
faq.a: Often. Commercial office carpet tends to be low pile, while home carpet can be much thicker, especially with padding. Measure rather than assuming a mat sold for offices will suit a home office.

faq.q: What size mat do I need on thick carpet?
faq.a: Cover the whole area your chair moves through, with some margin. The ES Robbins Everlife extra-high-pile mat (45 x 53 inches) and medium-pile mat (60 x 72 inches) are the largest options here.

bottomLine: If your carpet is over 1 inch deep including padding, the ES Robbins Extra High Pile mats are the only ones here rated for it; choose the standard size for a typical desk or the Everlife for more rolling room.

For carpet up to 3/4 inch, the Gorilla Grip and Marvelux polycarbonate mats are rated for the job, and the 60 x 72-inch ES Robbins suits large or shared desks. The MuArts and glass mats are reasonable on medium carpet, but they do not state pile ratings, so we would not rely on them for the deepest pile.
